stem: What does the -o option add to netstat -an?

options.text: The name of the user account that opened each connection
options.why: -o adds the process ID, not a user name.

options.text: The ID of the process that owns each connection (PID)
Only the connections that are open, hiding listeners
options.why: -o does not filter; it adds a column.

options.text: The amount of traffic sent over each connection
options.why: netstat does not show traffic volume here.

explain: netstat -ano shows addresses and ports as numbers, all states, plus the PID. Look the PID up in Task Manager or tasklist to find the program.

stem: What does the -n option do for netstat?

options.text: It shows only new connections and hides the ones that are already old
It hides the process IDs and the owning program names
It shows addresses and ports as numbers, with no name lookups
It shows only network statistics, not connections

explain: -n keeps output fast and unambiguous: you see real addresses and port numbers, not names.
